stemMd: A company says that its mentorship programme caused employees to remain longer because participants resigned less often than nonparticipants. Which finding most strengthens a selection-based alternative explanation?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Mentors held meetings once a month.

options.label: B
options.textMd: The company paid mentors a small allowance.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Employees planning to leave soon usually declined the invitation to participate.

options.label: E
options.textMd: The programme had a written handbook.

explanationMd: If people already intending to stay disproportionately join, the programme can appear effective even without changing anyone's decision. The finding links pre-existing retention plans to participation, supplying the alternative cause of the group difference.

distractorRationale.e: A handbook does not explain who joined.
distractorRationale.c: Mentors' history does not establish participants' prior intentions.
distractorRationale.b: Payment does not isolate employee retention effects.
distractorRationale.a: Meeting frequency does not establish selection bias.
